expectations.text: Pushes back on the 'are you sure?' modal as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: "I'd push back on the confirmation modal — here's why" and "Better approach: soft-delete + trash"

expectations.text: Explains habituation or click-through blindness as why frequent dialogs stop working
expectations.evidence: "Users develop muscle memory to click \"OK\" on modals, so you'll still get panic emails" and "harder to habituation-click"

expectations.text: Recommends reversibility (soft delete with a retention window) as the strongest option
expectations.evidence: "Delete → Archive", "30-day retention — workspaces auto-purge after 30 days", framed as "Better approach" / "replacement" rung

expectations.text: Recommends grace-period undo as a strong low-friction option
expectations.evidence: "Undo toast — \"Workspace deleted. **Undo**\" appears immediately after delete action"

expectations.text: Recommends type-the-workspace-name confirmation for the irreversible case
expectations.evidence: "If you must keep hard-delete... Require typing the workspace name (breaks muscle memory)"

expectations.text: If a dialog is retained, requires it to name the workspace and the scale of what is lost
expectations.evidence: "Show what will be lost (project count, last activity, team members)" plus typing the workspace name

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the deletion rules, not just the UI
expectations.evidence: No mention of server-side/API enforcement; all controls described are UI-level (modal, toast, trash view). Only 'sketch out the soft-delete schema design?' is offered, which is not an enforcement claim.

expectations.text: Gives an explicit preference order rather than an undifferentiated list of ideas
expectations.evidence: "Poka-yoke hierarchy: Elimination > Replacement > Facilitation > Detection > Mitigation" with soft-delete as primary and "If you must keep hard-delete" as the fallback tier
